items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1960-04-30
items.q: Then he made up this band. See, he consists of me, Eddie Pearson, Leo Desjard, Joe Phillips,

ctx.x: No, I mean, in 32 or so.

Oh, he broke up with P. the book out there. Yeah. He just quit the band. See, he quit the band with P. the book out there. Then he made up this band. See, he consists of me, Eddie Pearson, Leo Desjard, Joe Phillips, Arthur Durbney, Elliot Taylor, Manuel Sayles, and Simon Moreira. And a singer by the name of Harold Wells. That was his band. And we played together from 32 until 35. I did.
And I left the band in 35.

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-10-13
items.q: See, he had me, Eddie Pearson, Joe Phillips, Leo Dejon, Elliot Taylor, and Arthur Dudley

ctx.x: We'll put it on the next tape. You got time for one another half hour, huh? Yeah. Then I'll take you to the other building and run on down then. Oh, back to Piran. Who played piano with him when you were with him?

Well, when I was with him, he had a new band. See, he had got rid of Pete and all of that bunch. See, he had me, Eddie Pearson, Joe Phillips, Leo Dejon, Elliot Taylor, and Arthur Dudley, and Alavretta, Alexandra of piano. Oh, yeah. Sales, and Simon. See, that was his new band, you see.
Alfred Williams, what number reel is this?

items.title: Bob Watts Interview, 1963-02-28
items.q: You know, P. Ron used to tell Arthur Durbny, Leo Dejan when he was playing on the boat with Dirty Pope

ctx.x: Yeah? Well, that's the man that really caught over my eyes about the music, see, because Henry Red Allen, he'd get over there and he'd be teaching me something. I kept my little book, you know, I had Otto Langs. I never forget his trumpet method. And Henry, he'd teach me a little something in there, and then he'd know that I liked the blow show, and then he'd put on a little records. He'd get there with his trumpet. And I'd get mine. Oh, yeah, he was like Dipper. And me and him would copy records. Well, I didn't…

You know, P. Ron used to tell Arthur Durbny, Leo Dejan when he was playing on the boat with Dirty Pope, he used to tell them, say, man, why don't you put that music on the side? Try to memorize the music. Yeah. He was just looking at the music all the time. I suppose the lights go out. Yeah, that's right. And you know what happened? You see? And we was in the middle of a tune.
He said, now, didn't I tell you that? No, you can't play nothing. What happened, Gay? You can't play nothing. No, you see? The music automatically stopped.
